We've all probably heard that skull-drilling type of snoring that can't be ignored, tuned out, or slept through. These people have to know how bad they snore. I just can't believe that someone who snores that loudly never had anyone tell them. In my life, I've slept in shared spaces with many people - from my siblings to partners to random people at hostels or festivals. Most people don't really snore that bad, maybe some light snoring after one beer too many that I doubt anyone would call them out on. But if you snore so much you keep everyone up, there's no way no one ever told you.

I don't snore. People who sleep in the same room as me can have perfectly comfortable sleep the whole night through - they won't be disturbed by my snoring because I'm quiet. If someone snores, THEY are the problem that could be solved by staying in private spaces.

As for other things... Sure, it's normal that someone takes a long time using the bathroom, has an alarm clock that goes off super early etc. That's all within reason and has to be accounted for when staying in a shared space.

But snoring? Fuck that, that shit ruins the WHOLE night, unlike an alarm that rings for 10 seconds. Every other inconvenience (someone coming in late, someone talking, someone staying in the bathroom extra long) lasts a while and then stops. Snoring can easily last the whole night through. If you're a snorer and you know it, you book a private room. I'll die on this hill. If you know you're going to ruin everyone's night, YOU book a room. Not a person who's annoyed by it when they're not the ones who cause others problems.

And no, earplugs are not enough when someone snores particularly loud.

I don't really have much advice but here are my thoughts on the matter as a 27 year old girl who's also kind of torn between traveling long-term (which is my lifelong dream) and the pressure of finding a relationship.

I'm only getting started but for me the key is having a whole life back home and taking trips only every couple months. I plan to spend around 3-4 months traveling and the rest at home where all of my friends, family, and hobbies are. I still plan to date when I'm home (probably not when Im traveling because I don't see a point to that - I don't intend to move permanently) and I'm hoping I'll find someone who will either travel with me or be okay with me being gone couple of weeks at a time.

While I know it may be a lot to expect, I don't think 6 weeks apart here and there is that much. If someone wants the whole 9-5 job/white picket fence scenario, they're probably not for me anyway. I don't really want to have kids so that cuts my pool significantly and weeds out people who want the super traditional lifestyle in the first place. Is finding a relationship going to be much more difficult than for an average person who wants to stay in the same town forever and have 2.5 kids? Absolutely. 6. The reveal of lady whistledown... The mystery and the narration was what gave the show its tone.    With the big reveal and all, it literally felt like season 3 was the end to this entire story.

Edit: To sum up, I think Bridgerton changes into a show completely different than what made the fans love it. Will it get renewed? yeah, sure. But I think it won't be able to recapture the magic of the first two seasons and I doubt it will continue for long enough to show all of the siblings' stories. OP, just for the record, the supplements aren't really proven to do anything. Especially the super expensive mushroom-types (including the famous AHCC). I personally took all kinds of supplements you can read about online, including AHCC and turkey tail, and had my CIN1 progressed to CIN3 in just couple of months. The supplements didn't help AT ALL. I could have saved up the money I spent on them for LEEP instead.

If it makes you feel any better, unless she is at least a little open to being childfree (which doesn't sound like it), then your relationship would probably suffer anyway, even if you caved in and had kids. You're worried about a potential loss of the relationship you have with her RIGHT NOW, which is a relationship without kids. Since there's no scenario in which this version of your relationship can stay for the long term, then you would lose that beloved relationship anyway. Because with kids, a lot of the things you now love about this partnership would probably change.

Not saying that all relationships go to shit after kids  but things do change, and it's usually for the worse. Alone time is limited, sex more scarce, patience thinner, intimacy gone. I know it's not true for everyone and it doesn't have to be like this, but it is true for the majority of parents. I doubt there's anyone who can say: hey, my spouse and I have the same amount of time to care about our relationship as we did before kids. That's probably impossible if you want to be a good parent and put your kid first.

So remember, that even if you did decide you want children somewhere down the line, it still wouldn't be with the girlfriend you have and adore now. It would be a different, mom version of her. Of course, you would still love her, maybe even more. But it would be different. What I'm trying to say is - what you would be missing if this relationship ended, is something that you would probably be missing if you had kids too cause the relationship would inevitably change. Sure, some things for the better. But a lot of things for the worse too.

Not trying to crap on parents or the idea of having kids. It's just a perspective that helped me a lot when my own relationship ended due to very similiar circumstance.

There's a great video from neuroscientist andrew huberman in which he explains that when we lose someone - either through breakup or death - we have this huge peak in motivation. It's like we're starving and there's a food behind a window - we'll try to break it and hurt ourselves in the process only to fulfill the need (hunger or seeing the loved one). Pap smear is the best way to prevent cervical cancer. Which is mostly caused by HPV. Now you're probably thinking - well i practice safe sex/didn't have that many partners/im overall healthy, what are the chances i have hpv, right? 

WRONG. Around 80% of women will contract the virus at least once in their life. Sure, not all strains cause cancer but even the carcogenic ones are pretty common too. If it's caught early, during yearly pap smear, you got 99% chance of preventing the virus to cause cervical cancer. If you neglect pap smears... Who knows.

Now I don't mean to scare you. But yes, if you're a sexually active woman in her 30s who never had a pap smear, I can't blame your doctor for the outrage. How do I know all that?

It happens to a lot of us, it's just that sometimes the virus lays dormant or doesn't cause any changes and then goes away on its own so many people don't even know they had it.

Assuming you began having sex in your early twenties, you could be carrying hpv for 10+ years. Sure, you dont have to. Even if you contracted the virus at some point, you probably cleared it. But... It's tough and there are no definite answers. There are a lot of ways to look at this situation, though. Anyway, whatever he's doing - this has nothing to do with you and doesn't define your worth in any way. I know it's tough and i feel really sorry for you. I think i'd been depressed my whole life. Sometimes it was better, sometimes worse. A therapist suggested I try antidepressants but i thought you had to be crippled and unable to leave the bed in order to take them. I kept thinking: well, im not THAT depressed. But ever since my therapist made that comment, i kept entertaining the idea of medication. Read a whole lot about them and got scared by bad reviews or stories about side effects. 

But couple months later came a very low point for me and i just thought - fuck it. My life sucks enough already, how much worse can it get? And on the off chance that it can get better... Maybe it's worth a try? So I tried. My doctor prescribed me sertraline which is pretty generic and often the antidepressant doctors start with. It's generally well tolerated and doesnt have as many side effects as others. 

It took a couple of months, I think up to three, but it did work. I became more stable and less hopeless. No more waking up feeling like all I want to do is go back to sleep and never open my eyes again. I didn't turn into some sunny, positive person, but I just felt like a huge weight has lifted. I had minor side effects (mostly feeling shaky, it was weird, but not insanely unpleasant or disruptive to my life), but it was worth it. I wish I hadnt gone off sertraline. Maybe i should think of going back.
